decisions.reason: Changing clip duration from 30-90 seconds to 45-60 seconds does not alter the caption color, font, or effects requirements.
The duration change does not modify the clean-editing style or prohibition on distracting visual effects.
The source describes ongoing monthly production and does not change the historical extended-trial batch count, source content, or acceptance standard.
The ongoing 45-60 second duration rule does not modify the completed initial three-clip trial assignment.
Message 179 separately updates source material and moment-selection rules, and that same-message MODIFY is already present; the duration change requires no additional source-selection update.
Message 179 separately adds real points as acceptable self-contained moments, and that same-message MODIFY is already present; the duration range does not otherwise alter content completeness.
The target channels stated in message 179 are already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE and are not changed by the duration modification.
The source does not change or restate an effective-hook requirement; self-contained moment selection and clip duration are distinct constraints.
Message 179 reaffirms personal approval and quota counting but does not change the existing approval authority, rejection handling, or publication gate.
The 45-60 second duration rule does not change which clips may be published or the dedicated Instagram publication destination.
The duration change does not alter tracking coverage, tracked performance metrics, or transparency requirements.
The source's statement that an Instagram account will be provided does not change the existing requirement for a dedicated assigned account, and clip duration is unrelated.
